description: Single-panel tensile engineering stress–strain plot (Fig. 4). The x-axis is labelled "Engineering strain /%" (0–80, major ticks every 10); the y-axis is labelled "Engineering stress /MPa" (0–1200, major ticks every 100). An inset legend in the lower right lists four curves: ST (green), 550-6 (black), 600-6 (red) and 650-6 (blue). There is no scale bar and no data-point markers; this is a property plot, not a micrograph. The ST curve yields lowest, starting between the 300 and 400 MPa gridlines, work-hardens gradually to a broad rounded peak between the 700 and 800 MPa gridlines near 55–60% strain, and extends furthest, to about 72% strain. All three aged curves show strongly increased yield strength (starting between the 600 and 700 MPa gridlines) with much shorter elongation. 600-6 is the strongest, peaking just above the 1100 MPa gridline near 50% strain; 550-6 follows closely, peaking between the 1000 and 1100 MPa gridlines; 650-6 peaks between the 900 and 1000 MPa gridlines and then drops abruptly, terminating near 52–53% strain. The aged samples fail with little post-uniform elongation (near-vertical drop after the peak), whereas ST shows a long, slowly declining plateau. The figure demonstrates that aging raises yield and ultimate tensile strength at the cost of ductility, with 650-6 losing strength relative to 550-6 and 600-6.

observations.observation: The figure is a single tensile engineering stress–strain plot with x-axis "Engineering strain /%" spanning 0–80 (major ticks every 10) and y-axis "Engineering stress /MPa" spanning 0–1200 (major ticks every 100).
The lower-right legend lists exactly four curves with the exact labels ST (green), 550-6 (black), 600-6 (red) and 650-6 (blue).
The ST (green) curve has the lowest yield stress, starting between the 300 and 400 MPa gridlines, and the largest elongation, ending near 72% strain.
The 600-6 (red) curve reaches the highest peak stress of the four, rising slightly above the 1100 MPa gridline at roughly 50% strain.
The 550-6 (black) curve peaks between the 1000 and 1100 MPa gridlines near 50% strain, slightly below 600-6, and appears to cross the red curve at low strain (below ~10%).
The 650-6 (blue) curve peaks between the 900 and 1000 MPa gridlines near 50% strain and then falls abruptly to between the 800 and 900 MPa gridlines, terminating near 52–53% strain.

All three aged curves (550-6, 600-6, 650-6) begin from a yield stress between the 600 and 700 MPa gridlines, roughly doubling the ST yield level, and all fracture between about 50% and 58% strain with little post-uniform elongation.
No numeric strength or elongation values are printed on the plot; only the axis gridlines and the four legend labels are annotated.
The caption states the curves are tensile engineering stress–strain curves of the ST, 550-6, 600-6 and 650-6 samples.
The citing text states that the corresponding tensile property data are listed in Table 1 (i.e. exact values are not given in this figure).
The citing text states that all aged conditions show significant increases in both yield and ultimate tensile strengths but a reduction in ductility compared with the ST condition.
The citing text states that among the aged samples the 550-6 and 600-6 samples demonstrate superior strengths, whereas the 650-6 sample shows a marked reduction in strength.

The citing text attributes the strengthening primarily to precipitation hardening by intragranular κ-carbides interacting with dislocations, and the lower strength of 650-6 to grain-boundary weakening caused by serious intergranular κ-carbide precipitation.

subfigures.description: A single engineering stress–strain plot (no sub-panel labels) with x-axis "Engineering strain /%" 0–80 and y-axis "Engineering stress /MPa" 0–1200, containing four labelled curves: ST (green, lowest yield ~300–400 MPa, longest elongation ~72%, peak between the 700 and 800 MPa gridlines), 550-6 (black, high yield, peak between the 1000 and 1100 MPa gridlines), 600-6 (red, highest peak, just above the 1100 MPa gridline), and 650-6 (blue, yield similar to the other aged samples, peak between the 900 and 1000 MPa gridlines, abrupt drop near 52–53% strain).
